why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder's `npm test` maps to the existing script `node --test`. The files it names (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js) are all tracked. The verifier's checks 1 and 2 are `node --input-type=module -e "..."` with single-quoted JS strings inside a double-quoted shell argument. Their imports from './index.js' and 'node:assert/strict' are valid, and `; echo exit=$?` sits outside the quotes. In check 3, bash turns `\\\\` into `\\` and `` \` `` into a backtick. So JS receives `'^#{2,}\\s+`?'` and `'\\b'`, which make the regex `^#{2,}\s+`?name\b`. The `/^#{2,}\s/` literal and `'\n'` pass through unchanged. The `!` inside double quotes only matters in interactive shells with history expansion on, not in scripts. Check 4's `npm test; echo exit=$?` is valid. The repository facts don't show whether package.json has "type": "module", but the ESM commands work either way because `--input-type=module` sets the mode.
